title: Public display-reading fidelity audit
scope: Explicit lexeme-level audit of public candidates where the displayed kanji/proper-name spelling may not uniquely determine the palindrome reading.
principle: The normalized kana reading remains canonical for palindrome validation. Display ambiguity is a UX/fidelity issue, not a reason to alter a valid reading.

audited_lexemes.rationale: The displayed surname/place spelling does not by itself force the intended たかた reading. The palindrome depends on たかた.
The productive reverse-pair family uo-ou requires 魚=うお; the display may also be read さかな in ordinary Japanese.
The pair nushi-shinu requires 主=ぬし; the character has other lexical readings.
The palindrome family requires 種=たね; the character may have other readings in other contexts.
The app consistently uses いかわ, but proper-name readings are not guaranteed from orthography alone.

current_mitigation.remaining_gap: The display line itself does not explicitly tell the user which reading of an ambiguous kanji/proper name is intended.

recommended_rollout.phase1: Add lexeme reading-hint metadata and show a compact hint only for high-risk lexemes.
recommended_rollout.phase2: Keep medium-risk items metadata-only unless human review shows users frequently misread them.
recommended_rollout.preferred_ui: A small metadata pill such as 読み指定 高田＝たかた or 魚＝うお; do not rewrite the sentence display.
avoid: Changing the canonical kana reading to match a more common reading when that breaks the palindrome.
Adding furigana to every kanji candidate.
Demoting grammatical layer solely because a kanji has multiple readings.

next_step: Create a public reading-hint lexeme file for high-risk items, validate coverage, and integrate a conditional UI pill.
